notes: The baseline got the main boundaries right (single suspension owner, Pricing, Payouts, Billing) in 3 rounds and 77k tokens, and its map has no cycles. The acyclic result is partly the product of facilitator-proposed design choices the expert rubber-stamped: rate history moved into Finance's Pricing, an improvised LessonDelivery context run by the Scheduling team, and an improvised Marketplace team and StudentAccounts context. It never surfaced a rule like 'unpaid student can't book' (that fact was improvised in the skill run, not in the fact sheet). It breaks the trainer's rules on patterns. Internal relationships use Conformist almost everywhere: Scheduling CF to TutorVetting, Pricing CF to Reviews, Billing CF to Complaints, Payouts CF to Billing, and so on. That contradicts 'CF only towards a well-established language' and 'ACL downstream by default'. Some links have no ACL (StudentAccounts -> Scheduling/Billing, Complaints -> TutorVetting). Stripe is put behind an ACL even though the expert wanted to follow it as is. There is no discovery report and there are no canvases, and the final message is 711 words. No eval assertion checks the pattern quality of the relationships (C/S, ACL defaults); only the mechanical 'No Conformist between internal contexts' check catches it, so consider promoting it to a judgment assertion. Assertion 8 passes trivially here because there are no cycles, which is fine.
